text:
lina: Noticed a partner ELK ingest showing lots of base64 blobs that look like KMS ciphertext. They indexed it as `event.payload` and it's searchable. Example (trimmed): `CiQAMQ...base64...==` and a surrounding JSON that includes vault_wrap:true.

ben: Oof. Do we know whether those are wrapped ciphertexts or plaintext that was re-wrapped? If it's ciphertext, maybe lower risk but still needs key-policy review.

marcos: From KMS audit tailing: I see several Encrypt operations from our vault proxy and then UNWRAP calls from partner-project-logger at ~2026-04-08T04:12Z. That's odd. Ticketing in SEC-4012.

anya: Can you paste the log lines (redacted) and the ELK doc id? We need to correlate which pipeline forwarded them.

lina: ELK doc id: elk-2026-04-08-0b3f. Snippet: `{ "meta": {"service":"partner-shipper"}, "event": {"payload":"CiQAMQ...==", "vault_wrap": true, "orig_path": "gs://partner-logs/ingest/2026-04-07/obj.log"} }`

sec-bot: automated-alert: KMS audit shows UNWRAP by principal `partner-logger@partner-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com` using key `projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/sa-keys`. See internal ticket SEC-4012.

priya: If partner performed UNWRAP using our key, that implies cross-project IAM binding exists. We MUST check key policy and key ring IAM. Marcos, can you dump key IAM?

marcos: Running `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy sa-keys --keyring=infra --location=global --project=redwood` now. Quick look: there is a binding to `serviceAccount:partner-logger@partner-proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter. This is alarming.

ben: Why was that binding created? Was it intentional for a legacy partner setup? We need an audit of when and by whom.

lina: I found a terraform import commit in infra/terraform/2024-06 that added a `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding` for partner. Author is `ops-legacy-bot`. That predates current RBAC review.

priya: Immediate actions: 1) Remove partner decrypt privilege from the key (but do not destroy key). 2) Rotate any material that used the key as a live mitigation if we confirm plaintext was obtained. 3) Snapshot evidence to forensic bucket. Need legal/partner coord for data retention.

marcos: I'm pausing the IAM binding (applying a deny by removing the binding). Will snapshot policy and put it into gs://forensic-1787654321/iam-policy.json.

lina: Important: if ciphertext present in partner logs is original KMS-wrapped SA JSON, rotating the KMS key won't decrypt past ciphertext (unless they have old unwrap rights). But because they had unwrap rights, they could have gotten plaintext earlier. So we need to assume compromise until proven otherwise.

ben: Agree. We should also search Vault audit logs for any wrap/unwrap that targeted SA JSON blobs matching those base64 lengths. Use `vault audit` exports.

anya: Running a grep: `zgrep -h "CiQAMQ" /var/log/vault-audit/*.gz | head` returns matches from 2026-04-07T03:58Z coming from path secret/data/partner/ingest. Tagging results to SEC-4012.

sec-bot: automated-update: created incident channel #sec-4012, severity: high, evidence_bucket: gs://forensic-1787654321, owners: lina, marcos.

priya: RBAC question: do we have a policy requiring cross-project decrypts to go through an approval flow? If not, we should enforce via IAM automation and a policy gate. Opening PR to block wide decrypt grants.

lina: Also, ingestion pipeline has a rewrite hook that was supposed to scrub `private_key` fields. It looks like a regression allowed wrapped blobs through. I'll open an ingestion PR adding unit tests for no base64 KMS headers in fields.

marcos: For containment: removed partner decrypt binding, revoked any short-lived SA tokens we can find referencing partner-logger, and flagged partner org for immediate audit.

ben: Rotation plan: two parallel waves — KMS key rotation (schedule next-maintenance) and rotate any SA keys whose ciphertexts appear in logs. We need to avoid breaking partners who rely on the key. Coordinate with partner on a maintenance window.

anya: Quick forensics note: the base64 pattern includes a KMS header `CiQA` which maps to our key version v1. That helps timeline. We should extract all docs with that header and map by time.

priya: Legal question: partner contract allows we ask them to purge logs in case of sensitive data exposure? Jordan from legal needs to weigh in before we ask deletion. In the meantime, don't delete anything.

marcos: I'll create a locked forensic snapshot: `gsutil cp gs://partner-logs/ingest/2026-04-07/obj.log gs://forensic-1787654321/` and set ACL to security only.

lina: Action items: remove decrypt binding (marcos), snapshot evidence (marcos), add ingestion scrubber + tests (lina), open KMS rotation plan + partner coord (ben), run Vault audit search and list affected secrets (anya), legal + partner notification (priya).

sec-bot: automated-update: all containment steps in progress. Ticket SEC-4012 assigned. Next step: coordinate KMS rotation runbook.

ben: One subtle thing: rotating the KMS key will update key version but older ciphertext remains decryptable if key version still exists. We may need to rewrap secrets to new key version and revoke older versions. Runbook authored: `./runbooks/kms-rewrap.sh --key infra/sa-keys --from-version v1 --to-version v2`

lina: Also audit Vault for any consumers that directly write wrapped ciphertext into logs. We'll add a metric alert if logs contain base64 strings longer than 100 chars in `event.payload` to catch regressions.

priya: PR opened for IAM hardening: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1245 — blocks direct cross-project decrypt binds unless approved. Marking as emergency roll.

anya: I enumerated secrets under `secret/data/partner/` and found ~12 items with `service_account` keys. Flagging them for rotation. Posting list to forensic bucket (names only).

marcos: Removed binding and forced key.disableIamPolicyBinding for partner. Partner called back immediately asking why; I'm on call with them to explain we found possible exfil.

ben: Coordination note: schedule the KMS rewrap during low traffic and coordinate CI credential re-issue. Also bump alerting to P1 if any partner still has decrypt rights.

priya: After we rewrap and rotate, update vault roles to use rewrapped ciphertext and rotate SA keys. We'll also add short TTLs for wrap tokens.

lina: I'll draft a short incident update for legal + partner: timeline, actions taken, ask (don't delete until legal ok), and next steps. Sharing draft in 30m.

anya: Final immediate: I kicked off the rotate jobs for the 12 flagged secrets (dry-run first). Will report results.

marcos: Dry-run completed, no breakages observed. Ready to execute full rewrap once legal greenlights partner communication.

sec-bot: automated-update: SEC-4012 containment: bindings removed, forensics captured, rotate plan created. Next step: partner + legal review.

lina: Thanks team. We'll reconvene in the #sec-4012 channel after legal reviews partner note. Postmortem scheduled Thu 11:00 PT.
